newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures pare losses, end flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures pare losses, end flat to lower.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed unchanged to lower on Friday, paring earlier losses as strength on the CBOT overnight buoyed sentiment, local traders said.
Prices were steady to 40 yen lower, with the benchmark May 1998 contract down 40 yen at 15,980 yen per tonne.

All contracts fell during the morning session on technically driven selling by local investors, traders said. The market recovered later, as gains on the CBOT overnight encouraged investors to buy, they said.
The benchmark May 1998 contract is unlikely to fall significantly below the 16,000 yen level, traders said.

On CBOT Project A, the spot May corn contract was traded at $2.99 a bushel at 0650 GMT, up from $2.97 at Thursday's close. Spot May CBOT soybean futures were traded at $8.42 per bushel on the overnight trading system, up from $8.38-1/2 at Thursday's close.
